mainTopic: Heirs who swore falsely about their father's theft, the less-than-a-פרוטה rule, and רבא's series of questions about partial returns, shaving and sealing
overview: The amud opens by finishing a discussion of heirs who swore falsely about what their father stole: why do they pay the קרן but not the חומש? רב הונא בריה דרב יהושע says the father already stood trial, and there is no חומש for denying a lien on land. רבא instead says the item exists but was deposited with others, so the heirs' oath was honest. Next the גמרא returns to the משנה about owing less than a פרוטה. רב פפא is quoted in two versions on whether the thief must go after the victim when the item still exists and might rise in value. רבא rules that the value at the time of the theft decides, and brings support from the משנה about stolen חמץ after פסח. רבא then asks a series of questions that follow the same pattern: two bundles worth one פרוטה, a נזיר's last two hairs, and a half-sealed hole in a barrel. In the first two cases he concludes that nothing that counts is left, yet the מצוה act was not done. The barrel question is left unresolved after a proof from a משנה is rejected. The amud ends as רבא begins a new question about stolen חמץ, which continues on the next amud.

steps.title: The case is where the father already stood trial
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא explains that the heirs owe the קרן because their father had already been taken to court and found liable.
steps.simpleTranslation: The case is where the father already stood trial.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is answering a question from just before: how can the heirs owe the קרן for something their father stole? It answers that the father had already been taken to בית דין.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Once בית דין obligated the father, the theft became a fixed debt, like a written loan. A debt like that can be collected from the land the heirs inherited. That is why the heirs must pay the קרן.

keyTerms.meaning: Stood trial; was brought to court and found liable
The principal; the basic value of what was stolen

phrases.english: Where he stood trial.
phrases.notes: "He" is the father who stole. The court had already obligated him to pay before he died.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question raised just before this section about how heirs can owe the קרן.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The heirs should not owe anything for their father's theft.
steps.terutzMaskana: Since the father stood trial, the debt was fixed and can be collected from the heirs.

steps.title: Then they should pay the extra fifth too
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the answer: if the debt was fixed in court, the heirs should owe the חומש as well.
steps.simpleTranslation: If he stood trial, then he should pay even the fifth too!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the answer from Step 1. If the heirs truly owe this debt, then their false oath should also make them pay the חומש.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Someone who swears falsely about money he owes, and later admits it, pays the קרן plus a חומש. If the heirs really owed this money, their false oath should bring the full penalty. But the ברייתא says they pay only the קרן.

keyTerms.meaning: The extra fifth added as a penalty after a false oath about money

phrases.english: If it is where he stood trial,
he should pay even the fifth as well!

steps.triggerLanguage: אִי בְּשֶׁעָמַד בַּדִּין, אֲפִילּוּ חוֹמֶשׁ נָמֵי מְשַׁלֵּם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the answer given in Step 1.
steps.kashyaTarget: The explanation that the father stood trial
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If the debt was fixed, the false oath should bring the חומש as well. But the ברייתא exempts them from the חומש.

steps.title: No extra fifth for denying a debt backed by land
steps.stepSummary: רב הונא בריה דרב יהושע explains that the heirs owe no חומש because the debt rests on a lien on land.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב הונא בריה דרב יהושע said: Because one does not pay the fifth for denying a lien on land.
steps.whatsHappening: רב הונא בריה דרב יהושע defends the explanation from Step 1. The heirs owe the קרן, but their false oath does not bring a חומש.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The heirs owe this debt only through the father's land they inherited, since the debt has a lien on that land. The law of the חומש does not apply when someone denies a lien on land. So they pay the קרן, but not the חומש.

keyTerms.meaning: A lien; a creditor's legal claim on property

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב הוּנָא בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב יְהוֹשֻׁעַ:
phrases.english: Rav Huna son of Rav Yehoshua said:
Because one does not pay the fifth
for denying a lien on land.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב הוּנָא בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב יְהוֹשֻׁעַ לְפִי שֶׁאֵין מְשַׁלְּמִין חוֹמֶשׁ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge in Step 2.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: A fixed debt denied with a false oath always brings a חומש.
steps.terutzMaskana: A debt that rests on a lien on land brings no חומש when it is denied.
steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that the חומש penalty does not cover every kind of money claim. Denying a lien on land is left out.

steps.title: רבא: the item was deposited with others
steps.stepSummary: רבא explains the ברייתא differently: the stolen item still exists but was held by others, so the heirs swore honestly.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: What are we dealing with here? Where the father's sack was deposited with others. He pays the principal, since it exists. He does not pay the fifth, because when he swore he swore truthfully, since he did not know.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא gives a completely different explanation of the ברייתא. He does not need the case where the father stood trial.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In רבא's case the stolen item still exists, so the heirs must return it. That is why they pay the קרן. When they swore, they did not know about it, so their oath was not a lie. Without a false oath there is no חומש.

keyTerms.meaning: What case are we dealing with here? (a phrase that sets up a specific case)

steps.whatToRemember: Two explanations of why the heirs pay the קרן but not the חומש. רב הונא בריה דרב יהושע: the father stood trial, and there is no חומש for a lien on land. רבא: the item exists with others, and the oath was honest.

phrases.english: Rava said:
With what are we dealing here?
For example, where his father's sack
was deposited in the hands of others;
he pays the principal, since it exists,
he does not pay the fifth,
because when he swore, he swore truthfully,
since he did not know.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a different explanation of the ברייתא instead of the one in Steps 1–3.
steps.terutzResolutionType: A different way of setting up the case (אוקימתא)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The heirs owe the קרן only because the father stood trial.
steps.terutzMaskana: The item exists, so the heirs pay the קרן. Their oath was honest, so there is no חומש.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The ברייתא can be explained without the case where the father stood trial.

steps.title: רב פפא: if the item exists, go after the victim
steps.stepSummary: Quoting the משנה about less than a פרוטה, רב פפא limits it: the thief is exempt from chasing the victim only if the stolen item no longer exists.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'Except for less than a פרוטה's worth of the principal, etc.' רב פפא said: They taught this only where the stolen item does not exist. But if the stolen item exists, he must go after him, because we worry that perhaps it will go up in value.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to a new topic. It quotes the משנה's rule that a thief need not travel to return less than a פרוטה, and רב פפא limits that rule.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Usually a debt of less than a פרוטה is too small to require chasing the victim. But if the stolen item itself still exists, it could rise in value and become worth a פרוטה or more. So רב פפא requires the thief to go and return it.

keyTerms.meaning: The smallest coin that counts as money in halacha
To go after him; to travel to the victim to return it
We are concerned; we take this worry into account
It will go up in value

phrases.aramaic: חוּץ מִפָּחוֹת שָׁוֶה פְּרוּטָה בַּקֶּרֶן כּוּ׳.
phrases.english: Except for less than a perutah's worth of the principal, etc.
Rav Pappa said:

phrases.aramaic: לֹא שָׁנוּ אֶלָּא שֶׁאֵין גְּזֵילָה קַיֶּימֶת,
phrases.english: They taught this only where the stolen item does not exist,
but if the stolen item exists,
he must go after him;
we are concerned that perhaps it will rise in value.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic, going back to a later line in the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The exemption for less than a פרוטה applies only when the item no longer exists. If it exists, the thief must return it in person, since it may rise in value.

steps.title: Second version: no worry about rising value
steps.stepSummary: In another version, רב פפא says the thief need not go after the victim in either case, because we do not worry that the item will rise in value.
steps.simpleTranslation: Some say רב פפא said: It makes no difference whether the stolen item exists or does not exist. He does not need to go after him. We are not concerned that perhaps it will rise in value.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a second version of what רב פפא said. In this version he holds the opposite of Step 5.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Here רב פפא does not take seriously the chance that the item will gain value. So the משנה's rule covers every case: whether or not the item exists, less than a פרוטה does not require chasing the victim.
steps.confusionAlert: This is not a new אמורא arguing with רב פפא. These are two versions of what רב פפא himself said, and they reach opposite rulings.

phrases.english: There are those who say: Rav Pappa said:
It makes no difference whether the stolen item exists
or whether the stolen item does not exist,
he does not need to go after him;
we are not concerned that perhaps it will rise in value.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a second version of רב פפא's teaching that disagrees with Step 5.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Whether or not the item exists, the thief need not go after the victim for less than a פרוטה. The chance that it will rise in value is not a concern.
steps.whatToRemember: There are two versions of רב פפא. First: if the item exists, he must go after the victim because it may rise in value. Second: he never has to, because we don't worry about it rising in value.

steps.title: Three bundles that dropped in value must all be returned
steps.stepSummary: רבא rules that if someone stole three bundles worth three פרוטות and they dropped to two פרוטות total, returning two is not enough. He must return the third one too.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: If someone stole three bundles worth three פרוטות, and their price dropped so that together they were worth only two, then even after returning two bundles he still has to return the last one.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא gives a new rule about stolen items that lose value after they were taken.
steps.deeperAnalysis: After the price drop, the third bundle is worth less than a פרוטה, so you might think it no longer matters. רבא says it still has to be returned, because when it was stolen it was worth a full פרוטה.

keyTerms.meaning: They became cheaper; their value dropped

phrases.english: Rava said:
If one stole three bundles worth three perutot,
and they dropped in price and stood at two;
if he returned two of them to him,
he is obligated to return the other one to him.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רָבָא: גָּזַל שָׁלֹשׁ אֲגוּדּוֹת בְּשָׁלֹשׁ פְּרוּטוֹת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the topic of the less-than-a-פרוטה rule from רב פפא, now asking about an item that was worth a פרוטה at the time of the theft but dropped in value later.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The value at the time of the theft decides. A bundle that later drops below a פרוטה must still be returned.

steps.title: Support from the משנה about stolen חמץ after פסח
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings support from the משנה: someone who stole חמץ that then went through פסח can say to the owner, 'Here is yours in front of you.'
steps.simpleTranslation: And the משנה also taught this: If someone stole חמץ and פסח passed while he had it, he may say to the owner, 'Here is yours in front of you.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins a proof for רבא's rule by quoting a משנה. This step only quotes the source; the next step explains how it proves the point.
steps.deeperAnalysis: After פסח, חמץ that was owned during פסח becomes forbidden to benefit from, so it is worth nothing. Still, the thief may simply hand it back. The proof comes from what this implies, which is explained next.

keyTerms.meaning: And our תנא (the משנה) also taught this; a source that supports the statement
'Here is yours in front of you': the thief returns the item as it is and owes nothing more

phrases.english: And our tanna taught it too:
phrases.notes: This refers to the משנה earlier in the פרק, on דף 96b.

phrases.english: If one stole leavened bread and Passover passed over it,
he says to him: 'Here is yours in front of you.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a משנה to support רבא's ruling in step 7.
steps.raayaObject: רבא's rule that the value at the time of the theft decides
steps.raayaSupportSource: The משנה about stolen חמץ that went through פסח

steps.title: How the חמץ case proves רבא's rule
steps.stepSummary: The thief can only hand back the חמץ because it still exists. If it were gone, he would have to pay its original value, even though it is worthless now. The same applies to the third bundle.
steps.simpleTranslation: The reason he can just hand it back is that the חמץ still exists as it was. But if it no longer existed, he would have to pay, even though right now it is not worth money, because at first it was worth money. Here too, even though the bundle is not worth a פרוטה now, since at first it was worth a פרוטה, he must pay.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains the inference from the משנה and applies it to רבא's three bundles.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה lets the thief off only because the חמץ is still there to give back. That implies that if it were gone, he would owe its value from the time he stole it, even though it is worth nothing today. In the same way, the third bundle has to be returned because it was worth a פרוטה when it was stolen.

keyTerms.meaning: It still exists in its original form
At first; at the time of the theft

steps.whatToRemember: With a stolen item, its value at the time of the theft is what counts, not what it is worth now.

phrases.english: The reason is that it still exists as it was;
but if it does not exist as it was,

phrases.aramaic: אַף עַל גַּב דְּהַשְׁתָּא לָאו מָמוֹנָא,
phrases.english: even though now it is not worth money,
since at first it was worth money,
he has to pay;
here too,

phrases.aramaic: אַף עַל גַּב דְּהַשְׁתָּא לֹא שָׁוֶה פְּרוּטָה
phrases.english: even though now it is not worth a peruta,
since at first it was worth a peruta,
phrases.notes: The words in square brackets are the corrected wording; they spell out the step that matches the חמץ case.

phrases.english: he has to pay.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws the inference from the משנה quoted in step 8 and applies it to step 7.
steps.raayaObject: Value at the time of the theft decides whether payment is owed
steps.raayaSupportSource: The implied ruling of the חמץ משנה when the item is no longer there

steps.title: Two bundles worth one פרוטה, with only one returned
steps.stepSummary: רבא asks: if someone stole two bundles worth one פרוטה together and returned one, must he return the other?
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא asked: If someone stole two bundles worth one פרוטה together and returned one of them, what is the law? Do we say that now there is no stolen item left with him, because one bundle is worth less than a פרוטה? Or maybe he has not returned the stolen item he was holding?
steps.whatsHappening: רבא asks a new question about a case where neither bundle alone is worth a פרוטה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This differs from step 7. Here the leftover bundle was never worth a פרוטה by itself. One side says nothing that counts as stolen is left. The other side says the full stolen item, worth a פרוטה, was never actually given back.

keyTerms.meaning: He asked a question or dilemma

phrases.english: Rava asked:
If one stole two bundles worth one peruta together,
and he returned one of them to him, what is the law?
Do we say: now there is no stolen item here;
or perhaps, he has not returned
the stolen item that was with him?

steps.triggerLanguage: בָּעֵי רָבָא: גָּזַל שְׁתֵּי אֲגוּדּוֹת, בִּפְרוּטָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from bundles that dropped in value to bundles that were never worth a פרוטה individually.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether returning half of a theft worth one פרוטה exempts the thief from returning the rest

steps.title: רבא answers: no theft left and no returning
steps.stepSummary: רבא answers his own question: there is no stolen item here, and there is no returning here.
steps.simpleTranslation: Then he answered it himself: There is no stolen item here, and there is no returning here.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא answers his own question in a short, puzzling phrase that the גמרא will question next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The leftover bundle is worth less than a פרוטה, so it does not count as a stolen item. But 'no returning' is unclear at first, and the next steps clear it up.

phrases.english: He then resolved it:

phrases.aramaic: גְּזֵילָה אֵין כָּאן, הֲשָׁבָה אֵין כָּאן.
phrases.english: There is no stolen item here; there is no returning here.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question raised in step 10.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The leftover does not count as a stolen item, yet there is also no השבה.

steps.title: If there is no theft, there should be returning
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges: if there is no stolen item left, then the thief has returned everything that counts, so there should be השבה.
steps.simpleTranslation: If there is no stolen item here, then there is returning here!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רבא's wording because its two halves seem to contradict each other.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If what is left does not count as stolen, then the thief has given back everything he owes. That seems to mean he did complete the השבה. So how can רבא say there is 'no returning'?

phrases.aramaic: אִי גְּזֵילָה אֵין כָּאן – הֲשָׁבָה יֵשׁ כָּאן!
phrases.english: If there is no stolen item here, there is returning here!

steps.triggerLanguage: אִי גְּזֵילָה אֵין כָּאן – הֲשָׁבָה יֵשׁ כָּאן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the wording of רבא's answer in step 11.
steps.kashyaTarget: The phrase 'הֲשָׁבָה אֵין כָּאן' in רבא's answer
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Having no stolen item left seems to mean the return was complete, so saying there is no השבה looks like a contradiction.

steps.title: Exempt from paying more, but no מצוה of השבה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא explains that רבא meant: even though no stolen item is left, he has not done the מצוה of השבה.
steps.simpleTranslation: This is what he means: Even though there is no stolen item here, there is no מצוה of returning here.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא reads רבא's words in a way that removes the contradiction.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The thief owes nothing more, because the leftover bundle is worth less than a פרוטה. But the bundle he gave back was also worth less than a פרוטה, so handing it back does not count as doing the מצוה of השבה.

keyTerms.meaning: The מצוה of returning a stolen item

steps.whatToRemember: Owing nothing more is not the same as doing the מצוה. With two bundles worth one פרוטה, returning one leaves the thief exempt from paying more, but he has not done the מצוה of השבה.
steps.confusionAlert: 'הֲשָׁבָה אֵין כָּאן' does NOT mean he still has to return the second bundle. It means only that he did not do the מצוה of returning.

phrases.english: This is what he is saying:

phrases.aramaic: אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁגְּזֵילָה אֵין כָּאן,
phrases.english: even though there is no stolen item here,
there is no מצוה of returning here.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא in step 12 by explaining what רבא's words mean.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: 'No returning' seemed to clash with 'no stolen item.'
steps.terutzMaskana: He owes nothing more, but he did not do the מצוה of השבה, since what he returned was worth less than a פרוטה.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: Two bundles worth one פרוטה: after returning one, the thief owes nothing more, but he has not done the מצוה of השבה.

steps.title: A נזיר who left two hairs has done nothing
steps.stepSummary: רבא quotes a known rule: a נזיר who shaved his head but left two hairs has not fulfilled his shaving at all.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבא said: The Sages said that a נזיר who shaved and left two hairs has done nothing.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא states a known rule about a נזיר's shaving. This sets up the question he is about to ask.
steps.deeperAnalysis: At the end of his נזירות, a נזיר must shave his whole head. Two leftover hairs count as real hair, so the shaving does not count at all. This is the base rule for רבא's next question.

keyTerms.meaning: A person who took a vow of נזירות and must shave his head at its end
The Sages have said (quoting a known rule)
He has done nothing at all

phrases.english: And Rava said: The Sages said:
A nazir who shaved and left two hairs –
has done nothing at all;

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a second case from רבא built like his two-bundles question in Step 10.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A נזיר who leaves two hairs unshaved has not fulfilled his shaving at all.

steps.title: What if one hair is shaved and one falls out
steps.stepSummary: רבא asks: if, of the two leftover hairs, he shaved one and the other fell out, is that a valid shaving?
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא asked: If he shaved one and one fell out, what is the law?
steps.whatsHappening: רבא asks what happens when the two leftover hairs are later taken care of in two ways: one shaved, one falling out by itself.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The two hairs are now gone, but only one was actually shaved. The question is whether that is enough to complete the shaving.

keyTerms.meaning: He asked (raised a question he was unsure about)

phrases.english: Rava asked:
If he shaved one and one fell out, what is the law?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks a question built on the rule just stated.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Does shaving one hair while the other falls out complete the נזיר's shaving?

steps.title: Shaving one hair at a time is obviously fine
steps.stepSummary: רב אחא מדיפתי asks רבינא how רבא could be unsure. Shaving hair by hair is surely a valid shaving.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אחא מדיפתי said to רבינא: Is רבא really unsure about a נזיר who shaves one hair at a time?!
steps.whatsHappening: רב אחא challenges the question itself. He says the answer seems obvious.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A נזיר may shave his head one hair at a time, and it still counts as a full shaving. רב אחא reads רבא's case, shaving one hair and then the other one falling out, as just a version of shaving hair by hair. So why would רבא ask?

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַב אַחָא מִדִּיפְתִּי לְרָבִינָא:
phrases.english: Rav Acha of Difti said to Ravina:
About a nazir who shaved one hair at a time
is Rava asking a question?!

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַב אַחָא מִדִּיפְתִּי לְרָבִינָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רבא's question as having an obvious answer.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Shaving one hair at a time is clearly a valid shaving, so there seems to be no doubt to raise.

steps.title: The case is where one fell out first
steps.stepSummary: רבינא explains that רבא means a case where one hair fell out first and then he shaved the other. Maybe that is fine because less than the measure is left. Or maybe it is not a real shaving, since he never shaved a full two-hair amount.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: The question is needed where one of them fell out first and then he shaved one. Do we say that now, at least, there is no measure of hair left? Or perhaps this is not shaving, because at first he left two hairs, and now when he shaved there were not two hairs?
steps.whatsHappening: רבינא answers by narrowing the case: the hair fell out first, and only then did he shave the last one. Then he lays out both sides of the doubt.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Side one: in the end, no real amount of hair (two hairs) is left, so he is done. Side two: his first shaving failed because two hairs were left. His second shaving was of only one hair, which is less than the measure, so it may not count as a shaving at all.

keyTerms.meaning: It is needed only for a specific case
The minimum amount that counts (here, two hairs)

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up the order. The doubt only exists when the hair fell out first, so the shaving that came after was of only one hair.

phrases.english: He said to him: It is needed only

phrases.aramaic: כְּגוֹן שֶׁנָּשְׁרָ[ה] אַחַת מֵהֶן, וְגִילַּח אַחַת;
phrases.english: where one of them fell out, and then he shaved one;
phrases.notes: The letter in square brackets comes from the corrected wording, making it 'it fell out.'

phrases.english: Do we say: Now, at least,
there is no measure of hair left;

phrases.aramaic: אוֹ דִלְמָא, הָא לָאו גִּילּוּחַ הוּא –
phrases.english: or perhaps, this is not a shaving –
since at first he left two hairs,

phrases.aramaic: וְהַשְׁתָּא כִּי גִּילַּח לָא הָוֵי שְׁתֵּי שְׂעָרוֹת?
phrases.english: and now when he shaved, there were not two hairs?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רב אחא's challenge by limiting רבא's question to a specific order of events.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבא's case looked like ordinary shaving hair by hair, which is obviously valid.
steps.terutzMaskana: The doubt is when one hair fell first, so the later shaving was of less than the two-hair measure.

steps.title: רבא answers: no hair and no shaving
steps.stepSummary: רבא settles his own question: there is no hair here, and there is no shaving here.
steps.simpleTranslation: He then answered it: There is no hair here, and there is no shaving here.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא answers his own question with a short rule.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This uses the same wording as his answer about the stolen bundles in Step 11. The meaning is not yet clear, which leads to the next challenge.

keyTerms.meaning: He then went back and answered it

phrases.english: He then answered it:

phrases.aramaic: שֵׂעָר אֵין כָּאן, גִּילּוּחַ אֵין כָּאן.
phrases.english: There is no hair here, there is no shaving here.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question laid out in Step 17, in the same wording as Step 11.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: No hair is left, and also no valid shaving was done.

steps.title: If no hair is left, the shaving is done
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges: if no hair is left, then he has shaved everything.
steps.simpleTranslation: If there is no hair here, then there is shaving here!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא points out that רבא's two halves seem to contradict each other.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The goal of shaving is that no hair is left. If no hair is left, the shaving should be complete. So how can רבא say there is no shaving?

phrases.english: If there is no hair here –
then there is shaving here!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the wording of רבא's answer, just like Step 12 did for the bundles.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: No hair left should mean the shaving is finished, so saying 'no shaving' seems contradictory.

steps.title: No hair is left, but the מצוה of גילוח was not done
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא explains רבא's meaning: even though no real hair is left, he has not done the מצוה of גילוח.
steps.simpleTranslation: This is what he means: Even though there is no hair here, there is no מצוה of shaving here.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains the true meaning of רבא's words and ends this case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'No hair' means no amount of hair that counts is left on his head. 'No shaving' means he never did a proper act of shaving, since his last shave was of less than the measure. So the end result is fine, but the מצוה act is missing.
steps.whatToRemember: Just like the stolen bundles, the outcome can be complete while the מצוה act is missing. No real hair is left, but the מצוה of גילוח was not done.

phrases.english: This is what he means:

phrases.aramaic: אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁשֵּׂעָר אֵין כָּאן,
phrases.english: Even though there is no hair here,
there is no מצוה of shaving here.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Resolves the challenge in Step 19 the same way Step 13 resolved Step 12.
steps.terutzMaskana: 'No shaving' means the מצוה act of גילוח was not done, even though no real hair is left.

steps.title: A punctured barrel sealed by sediments is saved
steps.stepSummary: רבא quotes a rule: a barrel that got a hole, and sediments from inside then plugged the hole, is considered sealed again.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבא said: The Sages said: A barrel that was punctured, and sediments sealed it, has been saved.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא brings a new known rule about a sealed barrel. This sets up another question just like the last one.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A sealed clay barrel protects what is inside from טומאה. A hole ruins that protection. If the sediments plug the hole, the protection comes back.

keyTerms.meaning: A barrel (here a sealed clay barrel)
It was punctured, got a hole
They saved it (it counts as sealed again)

phrases.english: And Rava said: The Sages said:
A barrel that was punctured, and sediments sealed it –
they have saved it.
phrases.notes: Saved from טומאה: the barrel counts as sealed again, so what is inside stays protected.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a third case from רבא with the same opening words as Step 14.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A punctured barrel whose hole was plugged by its sediments counts as sealed again.

steps.title: What if only half the hole was sealed
steps.stepSummary: רבא asks: if half of the hole was sealed, what is the law?
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא asked: If he sealed half of it, what is the law?
steps.whatsHappening: רבא asks a question about a hole that was only partly closed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Now the hole is smaller than before, but it was never fully closed. Like the hair case, the question is whether a smaller leftover is enough, or whether the original problem was never fixed.

phrases.english: Rava asked:
If he sealed half of it, what is the law?
phrases.notes: Half of the hole, not half of the barrel.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks a question built on the barrel rule just stated.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Does sealing half the hole make the barrel count as sealed?

steps.title: רב יימר points to a משנה about plugged barrels
steps.stepSummary: רב יימר says רבא's question is already answered by a משנה, and quotes it. Sediments that seal a hole save the barrel. A vine plug only counts once clay is smeared around it. With two vines, clay must also fill the gap between them.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יימר said to רב אשי: Isn't this our משנה? We learned: a barrel that got a hole, and sediments sealed it, is saved. If he plugged it with a vine, it is not saved until he smears clay. If there were two vines, not until he smears from the sides and between one vine and the other.
steps.whatsHappening: רב יימר quotes the rest of the same משנה that רבא cited, because he thinks it already answers רבא's question. This step sets up the proof, which comes in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה separates two cases. When sediments fill the hole, the barrel counts as sealed right away. When someone pushes a vine into the hole, it does not count until clay is smeared over every gap.

keyTerms.meaning: Our משנה, the one we already have
He plugged it (stuffed something into the hole)
That he smears (clay around the plug)
They saved it, so it now counts as sealed

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַב יֵימַר לְרַב אָשֵׁי:
phrases.english: Rav Yeimar said to Rav Ashi:
Isn't this our Mishnah?
As we learned:
A barrel that got a hole, and sediments sealed it, they saved it.
If he plugged it with a vine, it is not saved until he smears.
If there were two in it,
phrases.notes: Two vine branches stuck into the hole.

phrases.english: not until he smears from the sides,
and between one vine and the other.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a source that seems to answer רבא's question from step 22.
steps.raayaObject: רבא's question about a half-sealed hole
steps.raayaSupportSource: The continuation of the משנה about a barrel plugged with a vine

steps.title: A vine without clay is like a half seal, so a half seal does not work
steps.stepSummary: רב יימר reads the משנה closely. The barrel counts as sealed only because the clay was smeared. A vine plug alone looks just like a half-sealed hole, so a half seal must not count.
steps.simpleTranslation: The reason is that he smeared; but if he did not smear, no. Why not? Let it be like he sealed half of it! So clearly, sealing half does not help.
steps.whatsHappening: רב יימר draws the proof from the משנה. A partly plugged hole, like a vine without clay, does not count as sealed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A vine fills only part of the hole, just like a half seal. Since the משנה demands clay before the barrel counts as sealed, a partial covering is not enough. That seems to answer רבא's question: a half seal does not help.

keyTerms.meaning: But if not (reading the opposite case out of the text)

phrases.english: The reason is that he smeared,
but if he did not smear, no;
Why not?
Let it be like he sealed half of it!

steps.triggerLanguage: טַעְמָא דְּמָרַח, הָא לָא מָרַח – לָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws the actual inference from the משנה quoted in step 23.
steps.raayaObject: That a half-sealed hole does not count as sealed
steps.raayaSupportSource: The משנה's rule that a vine plug needs clay smeared around it

steps.title: The cases are different: a vine will not stay, but a half seal does
steps.stepSummary: The חכמים reject the proof. A vine without clay will not stay in the hole, so it cannot count at all. A half seal made of something that stays put is a different case.
steps.simpleTranslation: They say: How can you compare? There, if he does not smear, it will not stay in place. But when he sealed half of it with something that stays, it does stay.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא rejects רב יימר's proof by showing the two cases are not alike.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The vine fails because it is loose and will fall out, not because it covers only part of the hole. A half seal made of a material that stays in place is solid as far as it goes. So the משנה tells us nothing about it, and רבא's question stays open.

keyTerms.meaning: How can you compare? (the cases are not alike)

steps.confusionAlert: Do not think the vine fails because it is only partial. The problem is that it will fall out, which is why it teaches nothing about a firm half seal.
steps.whatToRemember: The proof from the vine is rejected, so רבא's question about a half-sealed hole is left unanswered.

phrases.english: They say: How can you compare?!

phrases.aramaic: הָתָם – אִי לָא מָרַח לָא קָאֵי,
phrases.english: There, if he does not smear, it will not stay in place,
but when he sealed half of it,
with something that stays, it stays.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the proof brought in step 24.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects the proof completely, so רבא's question remains open
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The vine fails because it will not stay in place, not because it is a partial seal

steps.title: רבא: a robber of חמץ may return it after פסח as it is
steps.stepSummary: רבא quotes a rule. If someone stole חמץ and פסח passed while he had it, he may give it back as it is. He says to the owner, "Here is yours in front of you."
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבא said: They have said: if someone stole חמץ and פסח passed over it, he says to him, "Here is yours before you."
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to a new topic: another teaching of רבא, about a robber who stole חמץ.
steps.deeperAnalysis: After פסח, חמץ that was kept over פסח is forbidden to benefit from, so it has lost its value. Even so, the robber does not have to pay its value. Handing back the item itself is enough.

keyTerms.meaning: פסח passed while he had it
Here is yours in front of you (returning the item as it is)

steps.whyThisMatters: This rule is the base for the question רבא asks next.

phrases.english: And Rava said: They have said:
If someone robbed leavened bread
and Passover passed over it,
phrases.notes: After פסח this חמץ is forbidden to benefit from, so it is worth nothing.

phrases.english: he says to him: "Here is yours before you."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens the third 'וְאָמַר רָבָא, הֲרֵי אָמְרוּ' case (after Steps 14 and 21), the fourth in רבא's series of questions if you count the two-bundles question in Step 10. It uses the same חמץ rule cited in Step 8.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A robber of חמץ that became forbidden over פסח may return it as it is

steps.title: רבא introduces a question
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא announces that רבא is about to ask a question about the rule he just quoted.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא asked:
steps.whatsHappening: This is only a setup line. The גמרא is preparing for רבא's question, which comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The question itself does not appear yet. It will build on the rule about returning stolen חמץ after פסח.

keyTerms.meaning: He asks (raises a question that is not yet answered)

phrases.english: Rava asked:

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Introduces a question on the rule in step 26.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: A further detail about the stolen חמץ rule (the question comes next)
